prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the UK Conservative Party Manifesto 2005 (within 500 words)

Core vision and priorities
- Argues Britain is heading in the wrong direction under Labour; promises action, accountability and delivery.
- Governing values: reward hard work and responsibility; extend choice; devolve power to communities and professionals; secure a decent, safe society; reset EU relationship by repatriating powers.
- Focus on cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes; govern for all groups, oppose discrimination.

Economy, tax and pensions
- “Value for money” via £12bn annual savings by 2007–08: £8bn to reduce borrowing, £4bn to cut taxes.
- Match or exceed Labour spending on NHS, schools, transport, aid; more on police, defence and pensions; slower overall spending growth (4% vs Labour’s 5%).
- Lower taxes to promote enterprise; retain and raise minimum wage.
- Halve council tax for many pensioners (up to £500); restore earnings link for basic state pension; keep Winter Fuel Payment, over-75 TV licences; create Lifetime Savings Accounts; strengthen company pensions; use unclaimed assets to protect failed scheme members.
- Keep Bank of England independence; no Euro. Deregulate via regulatory budgets, sunset reviews; stop “gold-plating” EU rules; restore opt-out from the Social Chapter.

Families, childcare and education
- More flexible maternity pay; up to £50/week childcare support per under-5 via tax credits; support workplace nurseries and after-school clubs.
- Restore discipline: heads control admissions/expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; cut paperwork; funding follows the pupil; more school autonomy.
- Toughen exams (publish marks with grades), allow international qualifications; slim National Curriculum.
- 300,000 vocational grants (£1,000) for 14–16s; two hours after-school sport; ban junk food in schools; support school trips.
- Expand parental choice: 600,000 extra places first term; allow state-funded places at independent schools if cost-equivalent; moratorium on special school closures.
- FE reform; scrap university tuition fees; abolish admissions regulator; build university endowments.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS funding by £34bn over the Parliament; devolve control; abolish central targets, SHAs; reduce PCTs and quangos.
- “Bring back matron,” empower infection control, more single rooms; funding follows the patient; protect community hospitals.
- Recognise self-pay with a 50% NHS-cost contribution to cut waits; aim to end waiting lists within the Parliament.
- Partnership for long-term care to avoid forced home sales; more support for carers; reform dentistry access and payments.
- Health checks for long-stay non-EU migrants; STI public health campaign.

Crime, policing and security
- 5,000 extra police per year; elected police commissioners; cut paperwork; neighbourhood policing.
- 20,000 extra prison places; honesty in sentencing (serve full terms).
- Expand drug rehab to 25,000 places; reverse cannabis to Class B.
- Strong anti-terror approach with a Homeland Security Minister.

Immigration and borders
- British Border Control Police; 24-hour port surveillance; restore embarkation controls.
- Australian-style points system; annual overall immigration limit set by Parliament.
- Overhaul asylum: process claims outside the UK; take a fixed UNHCR quota; withdraw from 1951 Convention and repatriate asylum powers from the EU.

Accountability and constitutional reform
- Timetable for Action; sack ministers who fail to deliver.
- Abolish regional assemblies; return powers to councils; stronger select committees; cut MPs by 20%; seek largely elected Lords.
- “English votes for English laws.” Support devolution in Scotland; Welsh referendum on Assembly powers; uphold NI consent principle.

Communities, housing, transport, environment
- Devolve planning; tackle illegal traveller camps; devolve arts and Lottery funding.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership.
- Modernise roads; review all speed cameras; longer rail franchises.
- Protect Green Belt, prioritise brownfield; phase out HFCs; lower VED for low-emission cars; boost efficiency, recycling; diversify energy with renewables and efficiency.

Rural and agriculture
- Free vote to overturn hunting ban; honest British food labelling; require Red Tractor in public procurement; reform CAP; strengthen animal welfare.

Defence, foreign policy and Europe
- £2.7bn more than Labour on frontline by 2007–08; support service families; preserve regiments; keep NATO central.
- Transparent war decisions; remain committed to rebuilding Iraq; support a two-state solution in the Middle East.
- Oppose EU Constitution (referendum within six months); no Euro; restore Social Chapter opt-out; seek national control of fisheries; deepen CAP reform; support enlargement incl. Turkey.
- Meet 0.7% ODA by 2013; increase UK control over aid; champion open markets and rule of law.

Day One/First month actions
- Start recruiting extra police; bring back matron; first Budget to cut waste and taxes; empower heads to expel; initiate 24-hour port surveillance; set EU Constitution referendum date and campaign “No.”
